title: Best Ceiling Fan Under ₹1,500 in India (2026): 5 Budget Picks That Actually Cool
description: Compare the best ceiling fans under ₹1,500 in India by airflow, BEE rating, motor warranty and noise — five picks for bedrooms and one to skip.
short_desc: Five budget ceiling fans that move real air at under ₹1,500 -- and one popular model to skip.

headings.text: What actually matters in a ceiling fan under ₹1,500

cta.headline: Want the full spreadsheet?
cta.sub: Compare 25+ ceiling fans under ₹1,500 by CMM airflow, BEE star rating, motor warranty and noise.

faq.q: Are ceiling fans under ₹1,500 any good?
faq.a: Yes — brands like Crompton, Orient, Havells, Bajaj and Usha all sell reliable 5-star rated fans at this price. The trade-off is you skip BLDC motors (which cost ₹2,500+) and remote-control modules. For most Indian bedrooms, an induction-motor fan under ₹1,500 is a smarter buy than a cheap BLDC knockoff.

faq.q: What is the difference between a 3-star and 5-star ceiling fan?
faq.a: BEE 5-star fans use about 25-30% less electricity than 3-star fans. On a fan running 16 hours a day, a 5-star fan saves roughly ₹300-450 per year in electricity. The price premium for 5-star is usually ₹200-400 — payback in under 18 months.

faq.q: Should I buy a BLDC fan under ₹1,500?
faq.a: No — genuine BLDC fans in India start at ₹1,800-2,500. Anything marketed as BLDC under ₹1,500 is usually a marketing claim on an induction motor. Save ₹500 and get a better 5-star induction fan in this budget.

faq.q: What is the right sweep size for an Indian bedroom?
faq.a: 1200 mm (48-inch) is the right sweep for 95% of Indian bedrooms up to 150 sq ft. For larger rooms (180+ sq ft), go 1400 mm (56-inch). Smaller 900 mm fans are only for very small rooms or bathrooms.

faq.q: How long do budget ceiling fans last?
faq.a: A good induction-motor ceiling fan under ₹1,500 should last 8-12 years with normal use. The bearings usually need oiling or replacement at year 6-8. Crompton, Havells and Orient have the widest service networks for warranty claims.

tldr_pick: Our top pick is the Crompton HS Plus 48-inch at ₹1,299 — 230 CMM airflow, BEE 5-star rated, 5-year motor warranty, and the widest service network in India. For very small rooms (under 80 sq ft), the Usha Striker Galaxy 900mm at ₹1,099 is the right answer.
key_takeaways: BEE 5-star saves ₹300+/year: a 5-star induction fan pays back its premium in 18 months vs a 3-star.
Skip 'BLDC' claims under ₹1,500: real BLDC fans start at ₹1,800. Get a quality 5-star induction fan instead.
1200 mm is the right size for Indian bedrooms: only go 1400 mm for rooms over 180 sq ft.
who_for: Anyone furnishing a 1BHK or 2BHK on a budget, builders fitting fans in rental flats, and parents kitting out a kid's room. This is the sweet-spot bracket where Indian ceiling fan brands compete hardest — five solid picks under ₹1,500 means you don't have to compromise on air delivery or warranty.
methodology: We compared 25+ ceiling fans under ₹1,500 from Crompton, Orient, Havells, Bajaj, Usha and Polycab on Amazon India and Flipkart. For each, we evaluated airflow in CMM (cubic metres per minute), BEE star rating, power consumption in watts, motor warranty, sweep size, and reported wobble/noise complaints in customer reviews.
